propositions: Four dispatch call sites cast transport params to capability Protocols but lack runtime isinstance guards, relying on static type assertions with no runtime effect.
AttributeError raised when a transport lacks an optional capability is silently swallowed by broad exception handlers, conflating designed skips with real failures.
The safe assumption of single transport with all capabilities breaks under Data Center backend design where a second backend may legitimately not implement optional capabilities.

Runtime isinstance guards must precede capability-dependent calls and must report capability-absent scenarios distinctly through the existing bridge_alerts audit channel as designed skips, not failures.

A version-dependent hazard exists where Python 3.12's @runtime_checkable isinstance uses getattr_static and does not see proxied attributes, whereas Python 3.11 still uses hasattr, requiring a dual-check fallback for compatibility.
